purpose: Bounded reconstruction packets for a standard battle MVP. These are not Battle Runtime implementations and do not upgrade an external rule into local runtime proof.

packets.scope: ordinary player Basic / Skill resource gate only; no character-specific SP rules
packets.question: Who owns the shared battle-point state, and at which action boundary does a legal action consume or grant it?
inputs: team shared SP current and max
packets.selected_rule: Only a reconstruction candidate: reject a Skill when current SP is below its positive bp_need; a rejected action writes no SP. A future runtime must place a cost/gain at an explicitly named commit/completion boundary, never as an implicit selector side effect.
external_sources: Nanoka 4.4.54 Avatar 1105 and 1307: Basic bp_add=1, Skill bp_need=1
local_sources: data/raw/4.4.54/natasha_skill02_healhp_content_30.json: BySkillPointActivated exists but its context semantics are unrecovered
packets.evidence_level: R1 numeric facts + R0 mutation ordering
ordering_constraints: legality precedes any resource write
failure before an accepted commit must leave SP unchanged
the relative order of cost, effects, and completion is UNKNOWN
distinguishing_observations: Force an accepted Skill to fail after task start but before completion, then observe whether SP changed.
Observe the same action at full SP to distinguish grant clamp timing.
acceptance_fixtures: Natasha Skill 110502 bp_need=1 versus Basic 110501 bp_add=1
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Represent SP as explicit team state and require a packet-selected write phase. Do not hard-code an unproven phase.

packets.scope: ordinary Avatar Energy and Ultimate availability only
packets.question: How are Energy cap, normal-skill gains, Ultimate cost, gate, and write timing represented?
packets.selected_rule: Static reconstruction only: Natasha max Energy=90 and Black Swan max Energy=120; their Basic/Skill/Ultimate expose sp_base 20/30/5. Treat an Ultimate gate and its cost/write timing as unresolved rather than treating sp_base as a proven post-action mutation.
alternative_candidates: Ultimate gates at current >= max then spends before effects
Ultimate gates at current >= cost then spends at effect commit
Ultimate reserves cost then spends at completion
local_sources: No accepted local Energy holder/write artifact; only existing task/turn boundaries were reused.
packets.evidence_level: R1 numeric facts + R0 gate/write ordering
ordering_constraints: an illegal Ultimate cannot write Energy
gain/cost must be an explicit action-phase write
cap behavior and Ultimate post-use gain are UNKNOWN
unknowns: whether sp_base is the exact runtime gain at each action boundary
distinguishing_observations: Observe a full-Energy normal action to test clamp/write order.
Observe an Ultimate with current Energy exactly equal to its listed cap/cost and inspect pre-effect state.
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Keep Energy as per-actor explicit state with a phase-tagged mutation API; do not infer its writes from static sp_base alone.

packets.question: Can a real HealHP task traverse HealData to a positive CurrentHP state write?
packets.selected_rule: R4 local formula/emission rule: DispelStatus request precedes Heal request; FormulaType 4 yields max((MaxHP-CurrentHP)*percentage+flat, 0) times the ordinary heal factors. No rule is selected for positive CurrentHP mutation.
alternative_candidates: a HealData event listener writes clamped CurrentHP
DirectChangeHP mode 1 normalizes a positive heal delta
a delayed consumer writes after an event sequence
external_sources: Nanoka 4.4.54 Skill 110502 level parameters are a static amount reference only
hsr-optimizer heal amount rule is amount-only R2
packets.evidence_level: R4 through ordered request emission; positive consumer is absent
ordering_constraints: DispelStatusRequestBoundary before HealRequestBoundary
CurrentHP must remain unchanged until a separately proven consumer is invoked
DirectDamageHP negative path must not be reused as a positive-heal implementation
unknowns: consumer timing relative to event listeners
distinguishing_observations: Identify a native consumer receiving the constructed HealData, then show its property-10 write and its listener position.
A target at MaxHP distinguishes no-op, clamp, and queued-heal behavior.
acceptance_fixtures: existing core_real_skill_runtime_30_report: FixPoint(400) remains unchanged after a FixPoint(650) HealRequestBoundary
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Accept this packet only up to typed request emission. A production simulator must reject or mark unresolved any positive HealData state transition until the consumer packet exists.

packets.scope: ordinary player Basic, Skill, Ultimate and explicit single-target selection
packets.question: What minimal facts decide whether a player action and its target are legal?
packets.selected_rule: A reconstruction spec, not a client-complete selector: only the current living player actor may offer ordinary Basic/Skill/Ultimate candidates; resource gates are delegated to DYN-SP-CORE-01/DYN-ENERGY-CORE-01; single-target selectors use the locally proven task-context leaves once a target has been supplied.
alternative_candidates: target configuration resolves before action legality
legality rejects unsupported metadata before target selection
some requirements are deferred to task execution
packets.evidence_level: R4 selector leaves + R1 static metadata + unresolved resource packets
ordering_constraints: current-actor and alive checks precede target task execution
a null/ambiguous required target is not silently coerced
resource gate remains unresolved at its write boundary
distinguishing_observations: Run TargetConfig discriminator 12 against a context containing primary, adjacent, dead, and enemy entities.
Attempt a non-current actor action and inspect the client rejection boundary.
acceptance_fixtures: Natasha 110501 Basic, 110502 Skill, 110503 Ultimate metadata rows
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Provide a declarative legal-action model with an UNSUPPORTED outcome; do not expose a game-wide legal_actions API from this packet alone.

packets.scope: ordinary eligible action list, Turn/AV selection and advance
packets.question: Can one ordinary action complete, recharge, and lead to the next ordinary actor without guessing?
packets.selected_rule: R4 local rule for selection and advance: sort by recovered ordinary ordering, select first eligible actor, subtract selected delay from all admitted actors with floor zero, and advance elapsed delay. Completion is a real boundary, but next property-38 recharge must be supplied explicitly because its generic writer/formula is unrecovered.
packets.evidence_level: R4 selection/advance/completion boundary + R0 generic recharge
ordering_constraints: a subsequent TurnPrepare is forbidden while action phase is active
completion waits for native cleanup conditions, not only task success
recharge must precede a subsequent selection but its formula/writer is UNKNOWN
distinguishing_observations: Observe property 38 after an ordinary completed action without injecting a caller delay.
Use equal delays and compare repeated client ordering.
acceptance_fixtures: existing Natasha turn fixture: 10/20 delay selects Natasha then explicit recharge 30 selects ally
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Implement recovered advance exactly; require an injected semantic packet for ordinary recharge before claiming a closed action loop.

packets.scope: ordinary positive external amount to local TargetDamageHP/DirectDamageHP mode-0 transition
packets.question: Can an externally reconstructed normal-damage amount produce a constrained local HP state transition?
packets.selected_rule: Use the pinned external R2 amount evaluator only for a fully explicit input request, then hand a negative delta to the locally supported M507308 -> M504579 TargetDamageHP -> M506499 DirectDamageHP mode-0 path. This is EXTERNAL_RECONSTRUCTED amount plus LOCAL_STRUCTURAL_SUPPORTED HP mutation, not a local formula proof.
alternative_candidates: wait for unrecoverable PGOO evaluator dispatch
replace the local HP bridge with an external HP shortcut
ordering_constraints: amount construction precedes TargetDamageHP
each target traverses the recovered HP bridge
CurrentHP property write happens before unknown AfterPropertyChanged consumers
zero-HP consequence is handed off, not claimed
unsupported_cases: damage special mechanics not accepted by the external evaluator
distinguishing_observations: A live PGOO dispatch observation would only upgrade amount provenance; it is not required for this reconstruction boundary.
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Call an explicitly versioned external amount evaluator and the local HP transition as separate components, preserving both provenances in the trace.

packets.question: Which persistent state change makes an entity dead and removes it from target/action/timeline domains?
packets.selected_rule: No death rule is selected. The local HP path records a zero-or-below boundary only.
alternative_candidates: HP write directly toggles an alive flag
local_sources: data/semantics/4.4.54/direct_damage_hp_transition_12.json: NegativeHPRecordBoundary and AfterPropertyChanged are boundaries only
packets.evidence_level: R4 zero-HP boundary + R0 death transition
ordering_constraints: CurrentHP may be written at or below zero before the unknown consumer
no target/timeline cleanup order is proven
distinguishing_observations: Trace the first consumer after M506625 for property 10 where CurrentHP <= 0 and identify its persistent writes.
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Do not invent death state from CurrentHP alone; receive an explicit future death packet.

packets.scope: standard one-wave victory/defeat and wave transition
packets.question: When does exhaustion of a wave or player team become a terminal BattleState?
persistent_state_writes: NONE PROVEN for wave index or terminal result
packets.selected_rule: No terminal rule is selected. Static Stage->Wave->Monster order is reconstruction-ready, but dynamic exhaustion and terminal writes are not.
external_sources: Nanoka 4.4.54 Stage 30113121 has one wave, monster 4014030, and no Stage->Buff binding
local_sources: No accepted local terminal/wave runtime artifact
packets.evidence_level: R1 static scenario + R0 terminal semantics
ordering_constraints: wave/terminal checks cannot be silently placed before or after death/event processing
distinguishing_observations: Capture a one-wave standard battle at final-enemy zero HP and identify wave and terminal writes.
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Load static waves faithfully but keep terminal evaluation unavailable until a terminal packet is proved.

packets.scope: ordinary Toughness reduction and Weakness Break only
packets.question: How do toughness damage, weakness, zero threshold, break damage/status, and action delay compose?
persistent_state_writes: NONE PROVEN for toughness, broken state, break damage, or delay
packets.selected_rule: External evaluator can provide an amount only. No state-transition rule is selected for toughness or broken status.
alternative_candidates: delay occurs after all damage listeners
local_sources: No accepted toughness/break state transition artifact
ordering_constraints: external amount does not authorize a toughness decrement or break event order
distinguishing_observations: Trace a weakness-hit transition from toughness positive to zero and record all persistent writes/events.
acceptance_fixtures: STANDARD_DYNAMIC_FIXTURE_V1 uses a monster with static weakness/toughness metadata only
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Expose break amount as a separate reference calculation; do not mutate runtime stance from it.

packets.question: What event boundaries must exist in a standard action trace without recreating the full Event Bus?
persistent_state_writes: packet-specific; no generic Event Bus write is claimed
packets.selected_rule: Use named trace boundaries only: action_gate, action_begin, ordered_effect_request, effect_state_transition, post_property_changed_boundary, action_cleanup_complete, action_completion, terminal_check. Their existence is partly local; their generic listener ordering is not selected.
alternative_candidates: all effects synchronous in task executor
local_sources: direct_damage_hp_transition_12 records AfterPropertyChanged as a boundary
packets.evidence_level: R4 selected boundaries + R0 generic listener order
ordering_constraints: Natasha Dispel request precedes Heal request
CurrentHP writes precede unknown AfterPropertyChanged consumers
cleanup completion precedes next TurnPrepare
distinguishing_observations: For two listeners with competing writes, inspect their registration and invocation order in one concrete event path.
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: Use a small explicit transition trace, not a guessed general Event Bus. A listener order must be packet-backed before it mutates state.

packets.scope: only the singleton-skill ordinary Monster probe 8011010
packets.question: Can a real ordinary monster select a skill without claiming a general AI policy?
packets.selected_rule: For monster 8011010, the static candidate set contains exactly skill 801101001. Selecting that sole member is a set-theoretic singleton result, not proof of a generic priority or target policy.
alternative_candidates: AI chooses through a hidden state machine
local_sources: project index: Monster ComplexSkillAI paths are indexed but no parsed selection policy exists
packets.evidence_level: R1 static singleton candidate set; no dynamic AI proof
ordering_constraints: selection must occur only when the monster is the current eligible actor
target selection remains DYN-LEGAL-ACTION-01 unresolved
distinguishing_observations: Observe a multi-skill monster across equal and changed target states, then map the selection condition source.
acceptance_fixtures: atomic ordinary monster probe: 8011010 -> sole skill 801101001
packets.DSH_implementation_boundary: A simulator may use this one singleton probe for wiring only; it must not generalize the rule to other monsters.
